     9	# DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound
    10	
    11	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
    12	and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **finite dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`,
    13	there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**
    14	Weil divisors `D`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes:
    15	
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`:
    17	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.
    18	
    19	This is the **P5-uniform** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md`
    20	§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
    21	`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
    22	locus.
    23	
    24	## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)
    25	
    26	The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
    27	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
    28	`D₀ = 0`:
    29	
    30	* FLV-fiber at `D₀ = 0` (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) gives `n₁` with
    31	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;
    32	* `0 < deg F` (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`) makes `b := n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` a legal
    33	  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
    34	  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
    35	* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
    36	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
    37	  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.
    38	
    39	Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,
    40	and `b` depends only on `(Y, π)` — exactly the shape DAT-D consumes.
    41	-/

    61	/-- **DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound.** For a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`
    62	compatible with the structure morphisms, there is a single threshold `b : ℤ`, depending only on

    71	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1
    72	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    73	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    74	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    75	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
    76	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
    77	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
    78	  obtain ⟨n₁, hn₁⟩ :=
    79	    subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ (0 : Y.CurveDivisor)
    80	  have hd'pos : 0 < CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
    81	    zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor π
    82	  refine ⟨(n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) + 1
    83	      - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K), fun D hD => ?_⟩
    84	  -- the residual class `[D] · [F]^{-n₁}`
    85	  set c : Y.CechPic := CurveDivisor.picClass K D
    86	    * (CurveDivisor.picClass K (fiberWeilDivisor π) ^ n₁)⁻¹ with hc
    87	  have hcdeg : classDeg K c
    88	      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
    89	    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
    90	    ring
    91	  -- an effective witness of the residual class
    92	  obtain ⟨W, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
    93	  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    94	    have hWeq : CurveDivisor.deg K W
    95	        = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
    96	      rw [← hcdeg, ← hWc, classDeg_picClass]
    97	    linarith
    98	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hWdeg
    99	  -- the witness divisor `n₁ • F + E` is in the class of `D`
   100	  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)
   101	      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
   102	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_nsmul, hEc, hWc, hc,
   103	      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
   104	  -- base vanishing at `n₁ • F`, peel `E`, transport along the class
   105	  have hbase : Subsingleton
   106	      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
   107	    have h := hn₁ n₁ le_rfl
   108	    rwa [zero_add] at h

   110	      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)) 1) :=
   111	    peel_effective (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π) E hEnonneg hbase
   112	  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K hclass hpeel

   104	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   105	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = (g : ℤ)) :
   106	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧

   108	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
   109	  have hdegW : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) := by
   110	    rw [← classDeg_picClass K W, hW, hL]
   111	  have hentry : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) := by
   112	    rw [hdegW, hχ]; omega
   113	  obtain ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hentry

    11	
    12	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
    13	and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, the fiber
    14	twist `Θ₁ = fiberTwist π 1` (`RiemannRoch/FiberTwist.lean`) has degree exactly the degree of
    15	the fiber Weil divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`RiemannRoch/FLVFiberToolkit.lean`):
    16	
    17	`AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fiberTwist_one`:
    18	`classDeg K (fiberTwist π 1) = CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π)`,
    19	
    20	and, when `π` is moreover **finite** (hence surjective onto `ℙ¹`), this degree is strictly
    21	positive:
    22	
    23	`AlgebraicGeometry.one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one`:
    24	`1 ≤ classDeg K (fiberTwist π 1)`.
    25	
    26	This is the **Θ-positivity** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign
    27	(`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §2.4, §4 DAT-0b). It supplies FLV's `1 ≤ classDeg θ`
    28	threshold at every fibre — note that `deg Θ₁ = deg π` is **not** load-bearing on this route
    29	(worksheet §2.4); only positivity is needed.
    30	
    31	## The route (worksheet §2.4, pinned chain)
    32	
    33	`fiberTwist π 1` is `(fiberDivisor π 1).picClass`, the class of the pinned two-cover
    34	local-equation system `(t₀ on V₀, 1 on V₁)`. Its meromorphic presentation
    35	(`LocalEquations.presentation`) has trivializing element `t₀` on the chart `V₀` and the
    36	constant `1` on `V₁`; the associated presentation divisor
    37	(`Scheme.presentationDivisor`) reads off the orders of `t₀`, which by the fiber order table
    38	is exactly the fiber Weil divisor `F = (div u)⁺`:
    39	
    40	* `presentationDivisor_presentation_fiberDivisor_one`: the ord-of-`t₀` computation
    41	  identifying the two divisors, point by point via `Scheme.CurveDivisor.ext_coeffAt`;
    42	* `LocalEquations.presentation_picClass` + `CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor`
    43	  transport this to a class identity `fiberTwist π 1 = 𝒪(F)`;

    45	* `zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor` (surjectivity of the finite dominant `π`) gives `0 < deg F`.

/-!
# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover

The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
  have hmap :
      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    ext c
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    rfl
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
  rw [← hmap]
  exact h

/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
  · rfl

/-- The graph point of a field-valued point has residue degree one. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.residueDeg K (Over.graphPoint C t) = 1 := by
  exact residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
    (e := (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left)
    (by
      exact congrArg (fun q : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k K => q.left)
        (Over.sectionOfPoint_snd t))
    (by
      change (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) =
        (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base default
      exact congrArg (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base
        (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The graph presentation has multiplicity one at its graph point.

`presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations` initially records the multiplicity as an order.
The graph class and its residue field both have degree one, so the degree formula forces that
order to be one.  This is the pointwise input for finite-support class descent below. -/
theorem graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Over.graphPicClass C t =
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single (graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t) 1) := by
  let hx := graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t
  let a : ℤ :=
    Multiplicative.toAdd
      (Scheme.ordZ ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
        hx ((Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation.elem (Over.graphPoint C t)))
  have hsingle :
      Scheme.presentationDivisor K (Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation =
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a := by
    exact presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations C t
  have hclass :
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a) =
        Over.graphPicClass C t := by
    rw [← hsingle, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
    rfl
  have hdeg := classDeg_graphPicClass C t
  rw [← hclass, classDeg_picClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single'] at hdeg
  rw [residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint C t, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hdeg
  rw [hdeg] at hclass
  exact hclass.symm

/-! ## Image-set packaging -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/

/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.

The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}

/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
    (U : (relCurve C L).Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
    (rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L ∩ U).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hmem⟩ := Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints C L U hU
  exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨p, hp, rfl⟩, hmem⟩⟩

/-- Every point in the dense image has residue degree one, by its retained section certificate. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage'
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## Class descent for divisors supported on the rational-point image -/

/-- Every point in the rational-point image is non-generic.  The retained section certificate
identifies it with an actual graph point, where `graphPoint_ne_genericPoint` applies. -/
theorem ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) ≠
        genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left
  exact graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C _

/-- The one-point divisor at a base-changed rational point is the base change of a class on the
base curve.  This is deliberately a class statement: no pullback operation on Weil divisors is
needed. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hmem : x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx 1) =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hmem
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) = x at hpx
  subst x
  refine ⟨Over.graphPicClass C q, ?_⟩
  rw [← graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single C]
  exact graphPicClass_base_of_field C L q

/-- A divisor whose finite support consists of base-changed rational points has a Picard class
defined over the base field.

The proof folds the pointwise graph-class identity over the divisor's `Finsupp` support.  It
works for arbitrary integer multiplicities; effectivity and the prescribed drop degree are
orthogonal hypotheses used by the greedy reduction, not by class descent. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  suffices hmain : ∀ f : {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left} →₀ ℤ,
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
        (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
        coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) →
      ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L f =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c from hmain S hsupp
  intro f
  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero =>
      intro _
      refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
      change Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor) =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) 1
      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, map_one]
      rfl
  | single_add p b f hpf hb ih =>
      intro hsupport
      have hfp : f p = 0 := Finsupp.notMem_support_iff.mp hpf
      have hpMem : p.1 ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
        apply hsupport p.1 p.2
        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) p ≠ 0
        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same, hfp, add_zero]
        exact hb
      have hfSupport : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
          coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
        intro x hx hfx
        apply hsupport x hx
        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) ⟨x, hx⟩ ≠ 0
        have hxp : (⟨x, hx⟩ : {z : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
            z ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left}) ≠ p := by
          intro heq
          subst p
          exact hfx hfp
        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne hxp, zero_add]
        exact hfx
      obtain ⟨cp, hcp⟩ :=
        exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
          C p.1 p.2 hpMem
      have key : ∀ D : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor,
          (∃ cf : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L D =
              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) cf) →
          ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
              (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + D) =
              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
        intro D hD
        obtain ⟨cf, hcf⟩ := hD
        refine ⟨cp ^ b * cf, ?_⟩
        unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hcp hcf ⊢
        rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add,
          ← Scheme.picClass_single_zpow L p.2 b, hcp, hcf, map_mul, map_zpow]
      exact key f (ih hfSupport)

/-- Exact discharge of `SepClosedTranslatedDropData.baseSubtraction` for the rational-point
image.  The descended class is re-presented by an actual base-field divisor `Z`; at exponent
zero, the inverse of `chartTwistClass C 0 Z` is precisely `picClass k Z`. -/
theorem exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
          ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ :=
    exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq k c
  refine ⟨Z, ?_⟩
  rw [hc]
  apply congrArg
  simp only [chartTwistClass, pow_zero, one_mul]
  rw [hZ]
  exact (inv_inv c).symm

/-! ## The separably-closed drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Build the translated-drop package using the actual dense image of base-field rational
points.  Density, non-genericity, residue degree one, and the base-subtraction class identity
are derived here; only the lambda-tied positive-twist divisor and its degree/vanishing data
remain inputs. -/
noncomputable def sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ where
  m := m
  M₀ := M₀
  hM₀ := hM₀
  W₀ := W₀
  hW₀ := hW₀
  genusValue := genus C
  excess := excess
  hχ := chi_moduleKSheaf C
  hdeg := hdeg
  h1 := h1
  P := rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hdense := dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hPcl := ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C
  hPdeg := residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage' C L
  baseSubtraction := by
    intro S _ _ hsupp
    exact exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp

/-- Immediate lambda-tied consumer of the rational-point-image package.

The result contains the effective subtraction divisor, a base-field translating divisor,
`h⁰ = 1`, preservation of `H¹ = 0`, the class-level base-change identity, and the existing
`IsSplitWitness` for `μ` translated by that specific base-field class. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult_of_rationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ
      (sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
        μ m M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ excess hdeg h1)) := by
  exact exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult μ
    (sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
      μ m M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ excess hdeg h1)

end DropPackage

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-! ## The lambda-tied drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.

`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
  m : ℕ
  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
  genusValue : ℕ
  excess : ℕ
  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)

/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
base-field translating divisor.

The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
  translated : IsSplitWitness C
    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))

/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
rank-one witness.

The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
the conclusion. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
      hW₀, hSZ]
    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
      pow_zero, one_mul]
  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
  exact ⟨{
    S := S
    Z := Z
    nonnegative := hS0
    degree := hSdeg
    support := hSsupport
    baseClass := hSZ
    h0_one := hS0one
    h1_vanishing := hS1
    translated := htranslated
  }⟩

end DropPackage

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

    47	/-! ## The positive-twist input -/
    48	
    49	section PositiveTwist
    50	
    51	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    52	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    53	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    54	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    55	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

    62	base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
    63	call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated

   112	  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1

   160	      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   161	      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1

    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` (smooth of relative dimension one, proper and
    13	geometrically irreducible over the field `k`) and a field extension `K` of `k`
    14	(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file installs — **as instances that fire by typeclass
    15	resolution** — every hypothesis of the landed degree/Riemann–Roch stack
    16	(`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Degree`) for the base-changed curve

    18	`C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,

    21	exactly the `Over`-instance spelling that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver`
    22	uses (`.ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`), but keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`
    23	spelling that the Riemann–Roch files consume, rather than on the `relCurve C K` `def`.
    24

    26	(`Cohomology.SectionsBaseChange`): the second projection `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left` is the
    27	base change of the structure morphism `C.hom` along `overSpec k K ⟶ Spec k`. Every morphism
    28	property then transports by `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange` (smooth of relative
    29	dimension one, proper, geometrically irreducible), and integrality of `C_K` is
    30	`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced` applied to the base change (geometric
    31	irreducibility is transported; geometric reducedness comes for free from smoothness).
    32	
    33	## Main instances (keyed for the Riemann–Roch stack)
    34	
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instOverBaseChange` — item 1: `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is a `K`-scheme
    36	  via the second projection; `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K = (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`
    37	  definitionally (`baseChange_over_eq_snd_left`).
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft`,
    39	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperSndLeft`,
    40	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft` — the base-change transport of the
    41	  standing bundle onto the raw morphism `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` (item 2),
    43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperBaseChange`,
    44	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactBaseChange` (item 4) — the same properties in the
    45	  `↘`-spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K` that `classDeg` queries.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsIntegralBaseChange` (item 3): `C_K` is integral.
    47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange`,
    48	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange` (item 5): the two structure-sheaf

    12	/-!
    13	# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open
    14	
    15	The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
    16	open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
    17	to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
    18	sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
    19	sections on the original affine open are finite projective.
    20	
    21	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
    22	that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
    23	Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
    24	downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.
    25	
    26	This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
    27	the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
    28	either pinned theta chart.
    29	-/

    31	set_option autoImplicit false
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    36	open scoped TensorProduct
    37	
    38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    39	
    40	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
    41	
    42	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    43	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    44	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    45	
    46	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    47	
    48	/-- A compatible quasi-coherent module structure on the sections of a cocycle-glued
    49	line bundle over an affine open, together with its finite projective rank-one properties.
    50	
    51	The module instance is written explicitly in the fields so that it is definitionally the
    52	one induced by `qcoh`; a consumer may install `M.qcoh` and recover `M.finite` and
    53	`M.projective` without any proof-irrelevance transport. -/
    54	structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    55	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) where
    56	  qcoh : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V
    57	  qsmul_eq : ∀ {W : (relCurve C B).Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(relCurve C B, V))
    58	      (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op W)),
    59	      letI := qcoh
    60	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := D.sheaf) hWV r s =
    61	        gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit hWV r s

    63	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))

    65	    (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _
    66	    (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    67	  invertible : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    68	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    69	
    70	/-- Sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on every affine open admit a compatible
    71	invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
    72	pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
    73	descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/
    74	theorem nonempty_affineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    75	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    76	    Nonempty (D.AffineSectionsModel V) := by

    94	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
    95	  have hproj : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    96	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ m :=

    11	/-!
    12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
    13	
    14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
    15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
    16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
    17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
    18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
    19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
    20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
    21	
    22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
    23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
    24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
    25	provided on the carrier.
    26	
    27	## Main declarations
    28	
    29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
    30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
    31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
    32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
    33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
    34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
    35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
    36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
    37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
    38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
    39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
    40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
    41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
    42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
    43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
    44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
    45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
    46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
    47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
    48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.

    56	
    57	namespace Algebra
    58	
    59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
    60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
    61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
    62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
    63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
    64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
    65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
    66	  n : ℕ
    67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
    68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
    69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
    70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
    71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
    72	  comap_surjective :
    73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))

    79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
    80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
    81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
    82	
    83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
    84	  E.etale

    92	
    93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
    94	
    95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
    96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
    97	surjection. -/
    98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
    99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
   100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
   101	    EtaleCover A where
   102	  n := n
   103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
   104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
   105	  comap_surjective := by
   106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
   107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
   108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
   109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
   110

   112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafQcoh

/-!
# QcohOn for the m-chart glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1b, assembly)

The (P2) localization axioms and the quasi-coherence packaging of the glued sheaf
`gluedSheaf k U g` on a chart `V` under the **trivializing-family interface**
(`informal/spec-dat-1.md` decision (D3), in subordinate form): a finite family of basic
opens `D(h i)` (`h : ι → Γ(X, V)`) covering `V`, each contained in a gluing piece
`U (σ i)` (`hP : D(h i) ≤ U (σ i)` — containment, not equality, so that restricted
families serve smaller charts such as the pinned overlap).

* `exists_gluedRes_eq_gluedQsmul_pow` — **(P2) denominator clearing**: per-piece
  clearing (`IsAffineOpen.exists_res_eq_pow_mul`), finite uniformization of the
  exponent, defect annihilation on the affine double overlaps
  (`IsAffineOpen.exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero`), regluing in the sheaf, and a
  local comparison through `gluedSubmodule_ext`.
* `exists_gluedQsmul_pow_eq_zero` — **(P2) defect annihilation**: per-piece
  annihilation, finite uniformization, `gluedSubmodule_ext` against `0`.
* `gluedQcohOn` — the assembled packaging `Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V`
  (a `def`; keyed `instance`s are declared only at the pinned datum, stage 1d).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

section Assembly

variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule

variable {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens) (g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ)
variable {V : X.Opens} {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] {σ : ι → J} {h : ι → Γ(X, V)}

/-- **(P2) denominator clearing for the glued sheaf** on a chart with a trivializing
subordinate basic-open family: a glued section over `V' ⊓ D(q)` extends to `V'` after
scaling by a power of `q`. -/
theorem exists_gluedRes_eq_gluedQsmul_pow (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i))
    (hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i))
    {V' : X.Opens} (hV' : IsAffineOpen V') (hV'V : V' ≤ V) (q : Γ(X, V))
    (c : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen q))) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (e : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g V')),
      gluedRes k U g inf_le_left e =
        gluedQsmul k U g ((inf_le_left : V' ⊓ X.basicOpen q ≤ V').trans hV'V)
          (q ^ N) c := by
  classical
  haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  -- the pieces and double overlaps are affine
  have hPaff : ∀ i : ι, IsAffineOpen (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)) := by
    intro i
    rw [← Scheme.basicOpen_resHom hV'V (h i)]
    exact hV'.basicOpen _
  have hOaff : ∀ i i' : ι,
      IsAffineOpen (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')) := by
    intro i i'
    rw [inf_assoc, ← Scheme.basicOpen_mul, ← Scheme.basicOpen_resHom hV'V]
    exact hV'.basicOpen _
  -- the components of `c`, reshuffled onto the pieces
  have hpc : ∀ i : ι,
      (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)) ⊓ X.basicOpen q ≤
        (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen q) ⊓ U (σ i) := fun i =>
    le_inf (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right)
      ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (hP i))
  -- per-piece denominator clearing
  have hden : ∀ i : ι, ∃ (N : ℕ) (e : Γ(X, V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i))),
      X.resHom inf_le_left e =
        X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans (inf_le_left.trans hV'V)) q ^ N *
          X.resHom (hpc i) (c.val (σ i)) := fun i =>
    (hPaff i).exists_res_eq_pow_mul (inf_le_left.trans hV'V) q
      (X.resHom (hpc i) (c.val (σ i)))
  choose N₁ e₁ he₁ using hden
  set N := Finset.univ.sup N₁ with hNdef
  -- the uniformized clears
  have hden₂ : ∀ i : ι, ∃ e₂ : Γ(X, V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)),
      X.resHom inf_le_left e₂ =
        X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans (inf_le_left.trans hV'V)) q ^ N *
          X.resHom (hpc i) (c.val (σ i)) := by
    intro i
    refine ⟨X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans hV'V) q ^ (N - N₁ i) * e₁ i, ?_⟩
    rw [map_mul, map_pow, Scheme.resHom_resHom, he₁ i, ← mul_assoc, ← pow_add,
      Nat.sub_add_cancel (Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ i))]
  choose E hE using hden₂
  -- defect annihilation on the affine double overlaps
  have hann : ∀ i i' : ι, ∃ M : ℕ,
      X.resHom ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left).trans hV'V) q ^ M *
        (X.resHom (inf_le_left :
            V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i') ≤ V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i))
            (E i) -
          X.resHom (le_inf ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (hP i))
                (inf_le_right.trans (hP i')) :
              V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i') ≤ U (σ i) ⊓ U (σ i'))
              (g (σ i) (σ i') : Γ(X, U (σ i) ⊓ U (σ i'))) *
            X.resHom (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
              V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i') ≤ V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i'))
              (E i')) = 0 := by
    intro i i'
    refine (hOaff i i').exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero
      ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left).trans hV'V) q _ ?_
    have k₁ := congrArg (X.resHom (inf_le_inf_right (X.basicOpen q)
      (inf_le_left : V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i') ≤
        V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)))) (hE i)
    have k₂ := congrArg (X.resHom (inf_le_inf_right (X.basicOpen q)
      (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
        V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i') ≤
          V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')))) (hE i')
    have k₃ := congrArg
      (X.resHom (le_inf (le_inf (le_inf
          (inf_le_left.trans (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)) inf_le_right)
          ((inf_le_left.trans (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right)).trans (hP i)))
          ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (hP i')) :
        (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')) ⊓ X.basicOpen q ≤
          (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen q) ⊓ U (σ i) ⊓ U (σ i')))
      ((mem_gluedSubmodule_iff k U g
        (c.val : ∀ l : J, Γ(X, (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen q) ⊓ U l))).mp
        c.property (σ i) (σ i'))
    rw [map_mul, map_pow] at k₁ k₂
    rw [map_mul] at k₃
    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at k₁ k₂ k₃
    rw [map_sub, map_mul]
    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    rw [k₁, k₂, k₃]
    ring
  choose M₁ hM₁ using hann
  set M := Finset.univ.sup fun i => Finset.univ.sup (M₁ i) with hMdef
  -- the sections to reglue, through the piece trivializations
  have hglue₀ : ∀ i : ι, ∃ f : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i))),
      gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (inf_le_right.trans (hP i)) f =
        X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans hV'V) q ^ M * E i := fun i =>
    ⟨(gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (inf_le_right.trans (hP i))).symm _,
      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (inf_le_right.trans (hP i))).apply_symm_apply _⟩
  choose F' hF' using hglue₀
  -- the M-power defect equation, restricted to the gluing overlaps
  have hover : ∀ i i' : ι,
      X.resHom (inf_le_left :
          (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)) ⊓ (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')) ≤
            V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i))
        (X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans hV'V) q ^ M * E i) =
      X.resHom (le_inf ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (hP i))
            ((inf_le_right.trans inf_le_right).trans (hP i')) :
          (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)) ⊓ (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')) ≤
            U (σ i) ⊓ U (σ i'))
          (g (σ i) (σ i') : Γ(X, U (σ i) ⊓ U (σ i'))) *
        X.resHom (inf_le_right :
            (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i)) ⊓ (V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i')) ≤
              V' ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i'))
          (X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans hV'V) q ^ M * E i') := by
    intro i i'
    have hMle : M₁ i i' ≤ M :=
      le_trans (Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ i'))
        (Finset.le_sup (f := fun l => Finset.univ.sup (M₁ l)) (Finset.mem_univ i))
    have hM' : X.resHom ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left).trans hV'V) q ^ M *

    10	# The shared plus-class field collapse (DAT-B B-5 fibre collapse / B-4 gap-1 collapse)
    11	
    12	This is the **shared plus-class collapse lemma** flagged by `w4-datb-worksheet.md` §5
    13	risk 6 and by the B-4 landing note I-0252 ("state it once as a named lemma with a
    14	characterizing property … both consume it"): a plus class of the one-step étale-plus
    15	Picard group over a *field* becomes an honest relative-Picard class after base change to a
    16	suitable finite separable field extension.
    17	
    18	Over a field `K`, a plus class `p : PicEtAff C K` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented
    19	étale cover `E` of `Spec K` and a descent class `x` (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).  Field
    20	cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`,
    21	`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean` — étale covers of a field are refined by finite separable field
    22	extensions) supplies a finite separable `L/K` together with a `K`-algebra map
    23	`ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  Base-changing `E` to `L` yields a cover with an `L`-point, so the
    24	base-changed descent class is, by the descent/cocycle condition (`relPicAlgMap_congr`), the
    25	tautological datum of an honest class: `PicEtAff.map C L p` is the plus-unit of the
    26	relative-Picard class `relPicAlgMap ℓ x` on `C_L` (`PicEtAff.unit C L …`).
    27	
    28	## Main results
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` — the collapse: `mk C E x`
    31	  restricted over a finite separable `L/K` (via a `K`-algebra map `ℓ` of the cover
    32	  carrier) is `PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicAlgMap ℓ x)`.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom` — the same with the honest
    34	  class presented as `relPicMk` of a Čech Picard class `M` on `C_L`, the form the degree
    35	  seam (`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`) and the shifted-datum extraction
    36	  (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`) consume.
    37	
    38	The finite separable `L` with `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L` is supplied by field cofinality
    39	(`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`).  Both statements take the tower
    40	`k → K → L` as clean instance hypotheses — the campaign-idiomatic fibre-extension form
    41	(cf. `Picard/DivSchemeSeed.lean`).  A consumer must instantiate `L` with a well-behaved
    42	`Algebra k L` (a native tower); a `RingHom.toAlgebra`-composite `letI` triggers the
    43	two-level-tower diamond of I-0236 when `PicEtAff.map C L` unfolds the base-changed carrier

    91	  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk,
    92	    PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange L)
    93	      (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)))]

   102	    [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]

     9	# The unconditional splitting of a plus class over a field (CHART-U(a), input 1)
    10	
    11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.2 step 1 and `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 both
    12	open with the same move, and both treat it as a step of a longer argument:
    13	
    14	> restrict along `t`; a plus class over `κ(t)` is `PicEtAff.mk E x`; étale field-cofinality
    15	> produces a finite separable `L/κ(t)` over which the class is an honest Čech class.
    16	
    17	This file makes that move a **named, unconditional theorem** rather than a step, because it
    18	is consumed at three separate places (the split predicate `IsSplitWitness`, the coverage
    19	theorem COV-1, and the degree seam) and because its statement is exactly the *witness-free*
    20	half of `IsSplitWitness`: every plus class over a field becomes an honest Čech class over
    21	some finite separable extension.  Nothing here mentions a witness divisor, `H¹`, `θ`, `Σ`,
    22	`divRep` or a certificate.
    23	
    24	## Why this is worth isolating
    25	
    26	`IsSplitWitness C μ` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean:148`) is an existential over a *tuple*: the
    27	extension `L`, its four instances, the presenting Čech class `M`, and then the witness
    28	divisor.  Read naively, a consumer proving membership of `chartLocus` has to produce all of
    29	them at once, and a consumer *using* membership has to destructure all of them.  But the
    30	first six components exist for **every** class, with no hypothesis at all — that is
    31	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` below.  So the honest content of `IsSplitWitness` is only the
    32	witness clause *at* a splitting, and the two readings are related by
    33	`isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness`.
    34	
    35	That matters for the lane order: COV-1 (dat-b §1.2) can produce its splitting *before* it
    36	knows anything about `h⁰`/`h¹`, choose `m` at that field (§1.2 step 3, where the uniform
    37	bound genuinely does not exist), and only then run the drop.  Without this separation the
    38	`m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled inside one `∃`.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` — **every plus class over a field is an
    43	  honest Čech class over some finite separable extension.**  Unconditional; no witness.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEt` — the same in the `picEt` spelling, which is
    45	  the one `IsSplitWitness` is stated against.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` — the two readings agree:
    47	  `IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  Its `.mpr` is also the
    48	  introduction rule; see the closing note for why no positional constructor lemma exists.
    49	-/

   194	
   195	section Effective
   196	
   197	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   198	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
   199	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   200	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   201	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   202	
   203	/-- **An effective witness of a class of large degree.** If a Weil divisor `W` has
   204	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` then its Čech Picard class is realized by an **effective** divisor. The
   205	Riemann inequality (`riemann_inequality`) forces a nonzero global section `f` of `𝒪(W)`, i.e.
   206	`f ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `W + div f ≥ 0`; that shift is effective and of the same class
   207	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf`). -/
   208	lemma exists_effective_of_picClass (W : X.CurveDivisor)
   209	    (hW : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)) :
   210	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W := by
   211	  -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) ≥ 1`, so `H⁰` is nontrivial.
   212	  have hfr : 0 < Module.finrank K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) := by
   213	    have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
   214	      le_trans hW (riemann_inequality K W)
   215	    have : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) := by omega
   216	    exact this
   217	  haveI : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) :=
   218	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos hfr
   219	  -- a nonzero global section `g ∈ 𝒪(W)(⊤) ⊆ K(X)`.
   220	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0)
   221	  set s := (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
   222	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K W)) t with hs
   223	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
   224	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
   225	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
   226	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
   227	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
   228	    intro h
   229	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
   230	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
   231	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
   232	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
   233	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
   234	  refine ⟨W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
   235	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (W + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
   236	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
   237	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)
   238	    have htop : ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩
   239	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
   240	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
   241	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
   242	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   243	    omega
   244	  · -- same class
   245	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]
   246	
   247	end Effective

   249	/-! ## Effective peeling of `Subsingleton H¹` -/
   250	
   251	section Peel
   252	
   253	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   254	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
   255	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   256	
   257	/-- **Peeling one point.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(B))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(B + x))` along the
   258	landed dévissage surjection `H¹(𝒪(B)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(B + x))` (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` on
   259	`devissageSES`, whose skyscraper cokernel has vanishing `H¹`). -/
   260	lemma peel_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (B : X.CurveDivisor)
   261	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1)) :
   262	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   263	  set D : X.CurveDivisor := B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 with hD
   264	  have hBD : devissageDivisor hx D = B := by rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub, hD]; abel
   265	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
   266	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
   267	  have hsurj := Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
   268	  have hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (devissageDivisor hx D)) 1) := by
   269	    rw [hBD]; exact h
   270	  refine ⟨fun a b => ?_⟩
   271	  obtain ⟨a', rfl⟩ := hsurj a
   272	  obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ := hsurj b
   273	  exact congrArg _ (hsub.elim a' b')
   274	
   275	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point.** Iterating `peel_single`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A))`
   276	transports to `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A + n·x))`. -/
   277	lemma peel_nsmul_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (A : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
   278	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
   279	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   280	  induction n with
   281	  | zero => simpa using h
   282	  | succ n ih =>
   283	    have hstep := peel_single hx (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ih
   284	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
   285	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
   286	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
   287	    rwa [heq] at hstep
   288	
   289	/-- **Effective peeling.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(A))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(A + E))` for any
   290	effective divisor `E`: peel the finitely many points of `E` one multiplicity-block at a time,
   291	by induction on the size of the support. -/
   292	lemma peel_effective (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)
   293	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
   294	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) := by
   295	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E →
   296	      (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
   297	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) from H _ E hE rfl
   298	  intro n
   299	  induction n with
   300	  | zero =>
   301	    intro E hE hc
   302	    have hE0 : E = 0 :=
   303	      Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
   304	    rw [hE0, add_zero]; exact h
   305	  | succ n ih =>
   306	    intro E hE hc
   307	    classical
   308	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
   309	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
   310	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
   311	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
   312	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
   313	    have hbpos : 0 < b := lt_of_le_of_ne hb_nonneg (Ne.symm (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mp hp))
   314	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
   315	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
   316	      rw [hE', hb]
   317	      exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
   318	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
   319	      rw [hE']
   320	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
   321	      by_cases hq : q = p
   322	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
   323	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
   324	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
   325	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
   326	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]
   327	    have hrec := ih E' hE'nonneg hcard
   328	    have hsingle : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b = b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   329	      rw [CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb_nonneg]
   330	    have hsplit : A + E = (A + E') + b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   331	      rw [← hdecomp, ← hsingle]; abel
   332	    rw [hsplit]
   333	    exact peel_nsmul_single p.2 (A + E') b.toNat hrec
   334	
   335	end Peel

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic

     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
    13	
    14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
    15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
    16	
    17	## Contents
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
    20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
    22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
    24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
    25	  quasi-finite one.
    26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
    27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
    28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
    29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
    31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
    32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
    33	  docstring for the proof route.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` — the same finite `π`, now also carrying
    35	  **dominance**, exported from the transcendence step of the construction
    36	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1`). This is
    37	  the map the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing class form consumes with no external dominance
    38	  hypothesis.
    39	-/
    40	
    41	set_option autoImplicit false
    42	
    43	universe u
    44	
    45	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial
    46	
    47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    48	
    49	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
    50	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
    51	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/
    52	theorem IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    53	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
    54	    IsFinite π :=
    55	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g
    56	  IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite π
    57	
    58	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	
    60	section ZMT
    61	
    62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    63	
    64	/-- A locally quasi-finite `k`-morphism from a scheme which is proper over `k` to the
    65	projective line is finite. This is the Zariski-main-theorem half of the construction of the
    66	finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`: it reduces finiteness to local quasi-finiteness. -/
    67	theorem isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    68	    (π : X ⟶ P1 k) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = f) :
    69	    IsFinite π :=
    70	  have : IsProper (π ≫ P1.structureMap k) := hπ ▸ inferInstance
    71	  IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp π (P1.structureMap k)
    72	
    73	end ZMT
    74	
    75	/-- To produce a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹` it suffices to produce a locally quasi-finite
    76	one; Zariski's main theorem upgrades it. -/
    77	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
    78	    (h : ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, LocallyQuasiFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
    79	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
    80	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hcomp⟩ := h
    81	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hcomp⟩
    82	
    83	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    84	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    85	
    86	/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
    87	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
    88	
    89	This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
    90	
    91	Proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
    92	1. `C` is integral (smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.
    93	   GeometricallyReduced`, plus geometric irreducibility, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic`),
    94	   and the function field of `C` contains an element transcendental over `k`: the étale
    95	   coordinate of a standard smooth chart of relative dimension `1`
    96	   (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField`, via the structure
    97	   theorem for standard smooth algebras of Stacks 00T7);
    98	2. the transcendental function spreads out to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`: the stalks
    99	   of `C` are valuation rings (localizations of the Dedekind chart rings,
   100	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections` and `Curve.StalksDVR`), so at each point
   101	   either `f` or `1/f` is a regular germ; the two chart morphisms agree generically by the
   102	   gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`, so the associated rational map `C ⤏ ℙ¹` is
   103	   defined everywhere (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`);
   104	3. `π` maps the generic point to the generic point (transcendence again), hence has finite
   105	   fibers on the height-one Noetherian space `C`, hence is locally quasi-finite;
   106	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/
   107	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
   108	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
   109	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)
   110	
   111	/-- **Existence of a finite dominant map to the projective line.** On the smooth, proper,
   112	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` which is
   113	moreover **dominant**.
   114	
   115	The dominance is exported from the construction itself: the transcendental spreading-out
   116	`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1` sends the
   117	generic point of `C` to the generic point of `ℙ¹`, whose closure is all of `ℙ¹`. Zariski's
   118	main theorem (`isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite`) upgrades the locally-quasi-finite map to
   119	a finite one, preserving dominance and the compatibility with the structure morphisms.
   120	
   121	This is the FLV-4 frontier witness: it lets the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing headline and
   122	class form (`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`,
   123	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`) be
   124	consumed with the *constructed* `π`, with no manually supplied `IsDominant` hypothesis. -/
   125	theorem exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 :
   126	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ IsDominant π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
   127	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hdom, hcomp⟩ := exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1 C.hom
   128	  haveI := hqf
   129	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hdom, hcomp⟩
   130	
   131	/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line
   132	
   133	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
   134	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
   135	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
   136	affine), not how it was constructed. -/
   137

    13	there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**

    17	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.

    20	§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
    21	`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
    22	locus.
    23	
    24	## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)
    25	
    26	The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
    27	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
    28	`D₀ = 0`:

    33	  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
    34	  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
    35	* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
    36	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
    37	  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.
    38	
    39	Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,

    87	  have hcdeg : classDeg K c

    11

    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine

     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/

    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
