    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl

    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=

   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where

   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by

   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')

   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl

   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where

   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')

   172	variable (C) in

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneTranslatedCover
import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.SepPointsDense
import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TangentIdentitySection
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ClosedPoint

/-!
# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover

The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
  have hmap :
      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    ext c
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    rfl
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
  rw [← hmap]
  exact h

/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
  · rfl

/-- The graph point of a field-valued point has residue degree one. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.residueDeg K (Over.graphPoint C t) = 1 := by
  exact residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
    (e := (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left)
    (by
      exact congrArg (fun q : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k K => q.left)
        (Over.sectionOfPoint_snd t))
    (by
      change (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) =
        (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base default
      exact congrArg (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base
        (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The graph presentation has multiplicity one at its graph point.

`presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations` initially records the multiplicity as an order.
The graph class and its residue field both have degree one, so the degree formula forces that
order to be one.  This is the pointwise input for finite-support class descent below. -/
theorem graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Over.graphPicClass C t =
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single (graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t) 1) := by
  let hx := graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t
  let a : ℤ :=
    Multiplicative.toAdd
      (Scheme.ordZ ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
        hx ((Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation.elem (Over.graphPoint C t)))
  have hsingle :
      Scheme.presentationDivisor K (Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation =
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a := by
    exact presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations C t
  have hclass :
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a) =
        Over.graphPicClass C t := by
    rw [← hsingle, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
    rfl
  have hdeg := classDeg_graphPicClass C t
  rw [← hclass, classDeg_picClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single'] at hdeg
  rw [residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint C t, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hdeg
  rw [hdeg] at hclass
  exact hclass.symm

/-! ## Image-set packaging -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/

/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.

The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}

/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
    (U : (relCurve C L).Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
    (rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L ∩ U).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hmem⟩ := Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints C L U hU
  exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨p, hp, rfl⟩, hmem⟩⟩

/-- Every point in the dense image has residue degree one, by its retained section certificate. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage'
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## Class descent for divisors supported on the rational-point image -/

/-- Every point in the rational-point image is non-generic.  The retained section certificate
identifies it with an actual graph point, where `graphPoint_ne_genericPoint` applies. -/
theorem ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) ≠
        genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left
  exact graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C _

/-- The one-point divisor at a base-changed rational point is the base change of a class on the
base curve.  This is deliberately a class statement: no pullback operation on Weil divisors is
needed. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hmem : x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx 1) =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hmem
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) = x at hpx
  subst x
  refine ⟨Over.graphPicClass C q, ?_⟩
  rw [← graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single C]
  exact graphPicClass_base_of_field C L q

/-- A divisor whose finite support consists of base-changed rational points has a Picard class
defined over the base field.

The proof folds the pointwise graph-class identity over the divisor's `Finsupp` support.  It
works for arbitrary integer multiplicities; effectivity and the prescribed drop degree are
orthogonal hypotheses used by the greedy reduction, not by class descent. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  suffices hmain : ∀ f : {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left} →₀ ℤ,
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
        (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
        coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) →
      ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L f =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c from hmain S hsupp
  intro f
  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero =>
      intro _
      refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
      change Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor) =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) 1
      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, map_one]
      rfl
  | single_add p b f hpf hb ih =>
      intro hsupport
      have hfp : f p = 0 := Finsupp.notMem_support_iff.mp hpf
      have hpMem : p.1 ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
        apply hsupport p.1 p.2
        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) p ≠ 0
        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same, hfp, add_zero]
        exact hb
      have hfSupport : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
          coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
        intro x hx hfx
        apply hsupport x hx
        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) ⟨x, hx⟩ ≠ 0
        have hxp : (⟨x, hx⟩ : {z : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
            z ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left}) ≠ p := by
          intro heq
          subst p
          exact hfx hfp
        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne hxp, zero_add]
        exact hfx
      obtain ⟨cp, hcp⟩ :=
        exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
          C p.1 p.2 hpMem
      have key : ∀ D : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor,
          (∃ cf : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L D =
              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) cf) →
          ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
              (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + D) =
              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
        intro D hD
        obtain ⟨cf, hcf⟩ := hD
        refine ⟨cp ^ b * cf, ?_⟩
        unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hcp hcf ⊢
        rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add,
          ← Scheme.picClass_single_zpow L p.2 b, hcp, hcf, map_mul, map_zpow]
      exact key f (ih hfSupport)

/-- Exact discharge of `SepClosedTranslatedDropData.baseSubtraction` for the rational-point
image.  The descended class is re-presented by an actual base-field divisor `Z`; at exponent
zero, the inverse of `chartTwistClass C 0 Z` is precisely `picClass k Z`. -/
theorem exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
          ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ :=
    exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq k c
  refine ⟨Z, ?_⟩
  rw [hc]
  apply congrArg
  simp only [chartTwistClass, pow_zero, one_mul]
  rw [hZ]
  exact (inv_inv c).symm

/-! ## The separably-closed drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Build the translated-drop package using the actual dense image of base-field rational
points.  Density, non-genericity, residue degree one, and the base-subtraction class identity
are derived here; only the lambda-tied positive-twist divisor and its degree/vanishing data
remain inputs. -/
noncomputable def sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ where
  m := m
  M₀ := M₀
  hM₀ := hM₀
  W₀ := W₀
  hW₀ := hW₀
  genusValue := genus C
  excess := excess
  hχ := chi_moduleKSheaf C
  hdeg := hdeg
  h1 := h1
  P := rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hdense := dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hPcl := ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C
  hPdeg := residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage' C L
  baseSubtraction := by
    intro S _ _ hsupp
    exact exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp

/-- Immediate lambda-tied consumer of the rational-point-image package.

The result contains the effective subtraction divisor, a base-field translating divisor,
`h⁰ = 1`, preservation of `H¹ = 0`, the class-level base-change identity, and the existing
`IsSplitWitness` for `μ` translated by that specific base-field class. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult_of_rationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-! ## The lambda-tied drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.

`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
  m : ℕ
  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
  genusValue : ℕ
  excess : ℕ
  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)

/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
base-field translating divisor.

The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
  translated : IsSplitWitness C
    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))

/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
rank-one witness.

The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
the conclusion. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
      hW₀, hSZ]
    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
      pow_zero, one_mul]
  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
  exact ⟨{
    S := S
    Z := Z
    nonnegative := hS0
    degree := hSdeg
    support := hSsupport
    baseClass := hSZ
    h0_one := hS0one
    h1_vanishing := hS1
    translated := htranslated
  }⟩

end DropPackage

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

## Current endpoint (2026-07-30)

The earlier analysis below correctly proves that a legal index calibrated at a threshold `b`
has chart parameter `n = b`, but it silently specialised `b` to the *smallest named bound*
`B = M·δ + g`.  Vanishing is monotone: any `n ≥ B` is equally valid.  The declarations

`IsDivisorDegree C g` is not an obligation of coverage; it belongs only to the fixed-`B` branch
retained later in this file and in `Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed`.

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` settles that at a chart index legal at parameter
`n` the coverage hypothesis `hb` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` forces `b = n`, and
that `b = g` is false in general (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`).  Its item 3 then names the residue:
*reconcile the chart parameter with the threshold*.  Both that file and
`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s retraction treat the threshold `b` — DAT-0a's bound
**at the splitting field `L`** — as a per-`L` quantity that has to be obtained before the
reconciliation can even be stated.

**That is where the pricing is wrong, and this file measures why.**  Two separate points:

* **RETRACTED, 2026-07-30, by a fresh-context audit and reproduced by the author (inbox
  `I-1349`/`I-1350`).**  This bullet read: *"DAT-0a itself is not instantiable at `L` ... there
  is no `relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` anywhere in this tree, so a lane trying to instantiate DAT-0a at
  a splitting field is trying to build a morphism the project does not have."*  **That is
  false.**  `exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` (`Curve/MapToP1.lean:126`) *produces* such a
  morphism for any bundle satisfying the curve hypotheses, and
  `Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean` supplies those for `baseChangeBundle C L`
  (`instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft`, `instIsProperSndLeft`,
  `instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft`).  So DAT-0a *is* instantiable at a splitting field,
  in three `haveI`s.  The error was grepping for the arrow as a *term* when the answer was an
  `exists_`-producer quantified over curves — a producer census, not a term census, is what
  settles "no such morphism exists".
* **The threshold does not need DAT-0a.**  `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness`

## THE HEADLINE IS A RE-DERIVATION — read this before citing `subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound`

`subsingleton_h1_of_windowA_le_deg` (`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivFibre.lean:259`, landed

`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
*membership of the locus* needs.

The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-! ## The lambda-tied drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.

`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
  m : ℕ
  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
  genusValue : ℕ
  excess : ℕ
  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)

/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
base-field translating divisor.

The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
  translated : IsSplitWitness C
    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))

/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
rank-one witness.

The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
the conclusion. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
      hW₀, hSZ]
    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
      pow_zero, one_mul]
  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
  exact ⟨{
    S := S
    Z := Z
    nonnegative := hS0
    degree := hSdeg
    support := hSsupport
    baseClass := hSZ
    h0_one := hS0one
    h1_vanishing := hS1
    translated := htranslated
  }⟩

end DropPackage

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover

The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
  have hmap :
      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    ext c
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    rfl
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
  rw [← hmap]
  exact h

/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
  · rfl

/-- The graph point of a field-valued point has residue degree one. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.residueDeg K (Over.graphPoint C t) = 1 := by
  exact residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
    (e := (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left)
    (by
      exact congrArg (fun q : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k K => q.left)
        (Over.sectionOfPoint_snd t))
    (by
      change (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) =
        (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base default
      exact congrArg (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base
        (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The graph presentation has multiplicity one at its graph point.

`presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations` initially records the multiplicity as an order.
The graph class and its residue field both have degree one, so the degree formula forces that
order to be one.  This is the pointwise input for finite-support class descent below. -/
theorem graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Over.graphPicClass C t =
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single (graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t) 1) := by
  let hx := graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t
  let a : ℤ :=
    Multiplicative.toAdd
      (Scheme.ordZ ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
        hx ((Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation.elem (Over.graphPoint C t)))
  have hsingle :
      Scheme.presentationDivisor K (Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation =
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a := by
    exact presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations C t
  have hclass :
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a) =
        Over.graphPicClass C t := by
    rw [← hsingle, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
    rfl
  have hdeg := classDeg_graphPicClass C t
  rw [← hclass, classDeg_picClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single'] at hdeg
  rw [residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint C t, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hdeg
  rw [hdeg] at hclass
  exact hclass.symm

/-! ## Image-set packaging -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/

/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.

The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}

/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]

/-! ## Class descent for divisors supported on the rational-point image -/

/-- Every point in the rational-point image is non-generic.  The retained section certificate
identifies it with an actual graph point, where `graphPoint_ne_genericPoint` applies. -/
theorem ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) ≠
        genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left
  exact graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C _

/-- The one-point divisor at a base-changed rational point is the base change of a class on the
base curve.  This is deliberately a class statement: no pullback operation on Weil divisors is
needed. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hmem : x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx 1) =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hmem
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)

      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) = x at hpx

/-- A divisor whose finite support consists of base-changed rational points has a Picard class
defined over the base field.

The proof folds the pointwise graph-class identity over the divisor's `Finsupp` support.  It
works for arbitrary integer multiplicities; effectivity and the prescribed drop degree are
orthogonal hypotheses used by the greedy reduction, not by class descent. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  suffices hmain : ∀ f : {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left} →₀ ℤ,
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
        (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
        coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) →
      ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L f =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c from hmain S hsupp

  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero =>
      intro _
      refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
      change Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor) =

        apply hsupport p.1 p.2
        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) p ≠ 0

image.  The descended class is re-presented by an actual base-field divisor `Z`; at exponent
zero, the inverse of `chartTwistClass C 0 Z` is precisely `picClass k Z`. -/

    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
          ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹) := by

    exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq k c

  rw [hZ]

section DropPackage

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Build the translated-drop package using the actual dense image of base-field rational
points.  Density, non-genericity, residue degree one, and the base-subtraction class identity
are derived here; only the lambda-tied positive-twist divisor and its degree/vanishing data
remain inputs. -/
noncomputable def sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ where
  m := m
  M₀ := M₀
  hM₀ := hM₀
  W₀ := W₀
  hW₀ := hW₀
  genusValue := genus C
  excess := excess
  hχ := chi_moduleKSheaf C
  hdeg := hdeg
  h1 := h1
  P := rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hdense := dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L
  hPcl := ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C
  hPdeg := residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage' C L
  baseSubtraction := by
    intro S _ _ hsupp
    exact exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp

/-- Immediate lambda-tied consumer of the rational-point-image package.

The result contains the effective subtraction divisor, a base-field translating divisor,
`h⁰ = 1`, preservation of `H¹ = 0`, the class-level base-change identity, and the existing
`IsSplitWitness` for `μ` translated by that specific base-field class. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult_of_rationalPointImage
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
      PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ
      (sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
        μ m M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ excess hdeg h1)) := by
  exact exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult μ
    (sepClosedTranslatedDropDataOfRationalPointImage
      μ m M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ excess hdeg h1)

end DropPackage

    11

    13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage

    15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
    16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
    17	
    18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
    19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).

    22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
    23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
    24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.

    33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
    34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
    35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
    36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
    37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`

    66	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]

    74	/-! ## The bad locus is small: an admissible non-base point -/
    75	
    76	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    77	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
    78	/-- **An admissible non-base point** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 1): if `H⁰(𝒪(W))` is nonzero
    79	and `P` is dense (meets every nonempty open) and consists of closed points, then some
    80	`x ∈ P` is *not* a base point of the system: some nonzero section `f ∈ H⁰(𝒪(W))` has
    81	exact order at `x`, `(W + div f)ₓ = 0`.  The base locus is contained in the support of
    82	the base divisor `bd(H⁰(𝒪(W)))` — a finite set of closed points, whose complement is a
    83	nonempty open (it contains the generic point); the base-divisor achiever
    84	(`Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
    85	outside the support. -/
    86	theorem exists_admissible_nonbase_point (P : Set Y)
    87	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    88	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    89	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W)) :
    90	    ∃ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (_ : x ∈ P) (f : Y.functionField)
    91	      (_ : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0),
    92	      coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
    93	        = 0 := by
    94	  classical
    95	  set T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K W ⊤ with hT
    96	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 := by
    97	    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
    98	    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=
    99	      finrank_divisorSections_top K W
   100	    rw [hbot, finrank_bot] at hfr
   101	    omega
   102	  set B : Y.CurveDivisor := Scheme.baseDivisor K T W hTne with hB
   103	  -- the support of the base divisor is a finite set of closed points
   104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=
   105	    isClosed_biUnion_finset (fun p _ =>

   107	  set U : Y.Opens :=

   113	  obtain ⟨x, hxP, hxU⟩ := hdense U hUne

   117	  have hxB : coeffAt hx B = 0 := by
   118	    by_contra hne
   119	    exact hxc (Set.mem_iUnion₂.mpr
   120	      ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hne, rfl⟩)
   121	  have hBat : (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T W ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) = 0 := by
   122	    rw [← Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hTne hx]
   123	    exact hxB
   124	  -- the achiever realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
   125	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, hach⟩ :=
   126	    Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K (le_refl T) hTne hx
   127	  exact ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfT, hf, hach.trans hBat⟩

   129	/-! ## The exact drop at a rational non-base point -/
   130	
   131	/-- **The exact drop** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 2): at a closed `K`-rational point `x`
   132	(`residueDeg x = 1`) that is not a base point of `H⁰(𝒪(W))` — witnessed by a nonzero
   133	section `f` of exact order at `x` — and under `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`,
   134	
   135	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − x)) + 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W))`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − x)) = 0`.
   136	
   137	`≤`: sections of `W − x` are sections of `W` vanishing one order deeper at `x`, a proper
   138	subspace since `f` violates the deeper bound — one linear condition as `residueDeg x = 1`.
   139	`≥`: the χ-ledger gives `χ(𝒪(W − x)) = χ(𝒪(W)) − 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W)) − 1` and `h¹ ≥ 0`.
   140	Equality forces both conclusions — the induction invariant of the greedy drop. -/
   141	theorem h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase (W : Y.CurveDivisor)
   142	    (h1W : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
   143	    {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hdx : Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   144	    {f : Y.functionField} (hfW : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0)
   145	    (hnb : coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
   146	      = 0) :
   147	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + 1
   148	        = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) ∧
   149	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   150	  -- sections of `W − x` sit inside sections of `W` …
   151	  have hle : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   152	      ≤ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   153	    refine divisorSections_mono K ?_ ⊤
   154	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   155	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
   156	    by_cases hyx : y = x
   157	    · subst hyx
   158	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   159	      omega
   160	    · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   161	      omega
   162	  -- … properly: the exact-order section violates the deeper bound at `x`
   163	  have hfnot : f ∉ divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤ := by
   164	    intro hmem
   165	    have h0le := (mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf).mp hmem
   166	    have hcoeff := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp h0le x hx
   167	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   168	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self] at hcoeff
   169	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hnb
   170	    omega
   171	  have hne : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   172	      ≠ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   173	    intro heq
   174	    rw [← heq] at hfW
   175	    exact hfnot hfW
   176	  have hdrop : Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   177	      < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   178	    have hlt := Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_ne hle hne)
   179	    rwa [finrank_divisorSections_top K _, finrank_divisorSections_top K _] at hlt
   180	  -- the χ-ledger on both levels
   181	  have hchiW := chi_divisorSheaf K W
   182	  have hchiWx := chi_divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   183	  have hdegsub : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   184	      = CurveDivisor.deg K W - 1 := by
   185	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1, hdx,
   186	      Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   187	  rw [hdegsub] at hchiWx

   189	    Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 h1W
   190	  have hchidef : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   191	      = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ)
   192	        - (Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := rfl
   193	  have hh1 : Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) = 0 := by omega

   195	  haveI := moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)

   197	
   198	/-! ## The keystone: the greedy drop to `h⁰ = 1` -/
   199	
   200	/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):
   201	on the curve bundle `Y` over the field `K` with `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`, let `P` be an
   202	admissible point oracle — closed points, `K`-rational (`residueDeg = 1`), dense (meeting
   203	every nonempty open).  Then every divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`
   204	admits an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
   205	
   206	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`.
   207	
   208	Induction on `e`: at each step the rank anchor gives `h⁰ = e' + 1 ≥ 1`, the oracle
   209	supplies a rational non-base point (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`), and the exact
   210	drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while
   211	lowering the degree budget by one.  The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5) instantiates
   212	`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
   213	theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
   214	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   215	    (P : Set Y)
   216	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   217	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
   218	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   219	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (e : ℕ)
   220	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e)
   221	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   222	    ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   223	      (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   224	      Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   225	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) := by
   226	  suffices H : ∀ (e : ℕ) (W : Y.CurveDivisor),
   227	      CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e →
   228	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →
   229	      ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   230	        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   231	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   232	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
   233	    H e W hdeg h1
   234	  intro e
   235	  induction e with
   236	  | zero =>
   237	    intro W hdeg h1
   238	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   239	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   240	    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   241	    · intro x hx hne
   242	      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
   243	    · rw [sub_zero]
   244	      push_cast at hanchor
   245	      omega
   246	    · rw [sub_zero]
   247	      exact h1
   248	  | succ e ih =>
   249	    intro W hdeg h1
   250	    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
   251	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   252	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   253	    have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   254	      push_cast at hanchor
   255	      omega
   256	    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
   257	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
   258	      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos
   259	    obtain ⟨hdrop, h1'⟩ :=
   260	      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
   261	    have hdeg' : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = (g : ℤ) + e := by
   262	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   263	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one, hdeg]
   264	      push_cast
   265	      ring
   266	    obtain ⟨S', hS'0, hS'deg, hS'P, hS'h0, hS'h1⟩ :=
   267	      ih (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) hdeg' h1'
   268	    have hsplit : W - (S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   269	        = W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - S' := by
   270	      abel
   271	    refine ⟨S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   272	    · -- effectivity
   273	      refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   274	      have h0S' := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hS'0 y hy
   275	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h0S'
   276	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   277	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   278	      · subst hyx
   279	        rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   280	        omega
   281	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   282	        omega
   283	    · -- degree
   284	      rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, hS'deg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   285	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   286	      push_cast
   287	      ring
   288	    · -- support in `P`
   289	      intro y hy hne
   290	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hne
   291	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   292	      · subst hyx
   293	        exact hxP
   294	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx, add_zero] at hne
   295	        exact hS'P y hy hne
   296	    · rw [hsplit]
   297	      exact hS'h0
   298	    · rw [hsplit]
   299	      exact hS'h1

    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine

    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :

    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),

    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocus
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The unconditional splitting of a plus class over a field (CHART-U(a), input 1)
    10	
    11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.2 step 1 and `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 both
    12	open with the same move, and both treat it as a step of a longer argument:
    13	
    14	> restrict along `t`; a plus class over `κ(t)` is `PicEtAff.mk E x`; étale field-cofinality
    15	> produces a finite separable `L/κ(t)` over which the class is an honest Čech class.
    16	
    17	This file makes that move a **named, unconditional theorem** rather than a step, because it
    18	is consumed at three separate places (the split predicate `IsSplitWitness`, the coverage
    19	theorem COV-1, and the degree seam) and because its statement is exactly the *witness-free*
    20	half of `IsSplitWitness`: every plus class over a field becomes an honest Čech class over
    21	some finite separable extension.  Nothing here mentions a witness divisor, `H¹`, `θ`, `Σ`,
    22	`divRep` or a certificate.
    23	
    24	## Why this is worth isolating
    25	
    26	`IsSplitWitness C μ` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean:148`) is an existential over a *tuple*: the
    27	extension `L`, its four instances, the presenting Čech class `M`, and then the witness
    28	divisor.  Read naively, a consumer proving membership of `chartLocus` has to produce all of
    29	them at once, and a consumer *using* membership has to destructure all of them.  But the
    30	first six components exist for **every** class, with no hypothesis at all — that is
    31	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` below.  So the honest content of `IsSplitWitness` is only the
    32	witness clause *at* a splitting, and the two readings are related by
    33	`isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness`.
    34	
    35	That matters for the lane order: COV-1 (dat-b §1.2) can produce its splitting *before* it
    36	knows anything about `h⁰`/`h¹`, choose `m` at that field (§1.2 step 3, where the uniform
    37	bound genuinely does not exist), and only then run the drop.  Without this separation the
    38	`m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled inside one `∃`.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` — **every plus class over a field is an
    43	  honest Čech class over some finite separable extension.**  Unconditional; no witness.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEt` — the same in the `picEt` spelling, which is
    45	  the one `IsSplitWitness` is stated against.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` — the two readings agree:
    47	  `IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  Its `.mpr` is also the
    48	  introduction rule; see the closing note for why no positional constructor lemma exists.
    49	-/
    50	
    51	set_option autoImplicit false
    52	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    53	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    54	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
    55	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    56	
    57	universe u
    58	
    59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    60	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
    61	
    62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    63	
    64	open AlgebraicJacobian
    65	
    66	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    67	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	noncomputable section
    74	
    75	/-! ## The splitting itself -/
    76	
    77	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    78	-- The presentation lives over the base-changed étale carrier, and closing the existential
    79	-- unifies its `Algebra k L` (the derived composite) against the goal's through that carrier
    80	-- — the same heavy defeq `PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean` budgets 800000 for.
    81	/-- **Every plus class over a field is an honest Čech class over some finite separable
    82	extension** (`w4-datb` §1.2 step 1, `w4-datc` §3.3 — the first move of both, here
    83	unconditional and witness-free).
    84	
    85	Given `μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)`, there is a finite separable `L/K` and a Čech Picard
    86	class `M` on `C_L` with `μ|_L = relPicMk M` as plus classes.
    87	
    88	The three steps, each a landed brick:
    89	
    90	1. `picEtAffineEquiv` (`Picard/PicEt.lean:235`) reads `μ` in `PicEtAff C K`, where by
    91	   `PicEtAff.ind` it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented étale cover `E` of `K` and a
    92	   descent class `x`;
    93	2. étale field-cofinality — `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`
    94	   (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`) — refines `E` by a finite separable field `L/K`,
    95	   i.e. supplies `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  This is the step that uses that `K` is a
    96	   *field*: over a general base an étale cover has no such refinement;
    97	3. `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:101`)
    98	   converts the refinement into the presentation.
    99	
   100	The `k`-algebra structure on `L` and the tower `k → K → L` are *derived*, not chosen: they
   101	are the composite `algebraMap K L ∘ algebraMap k K`, exactly as `degAffFieldAlgebraBase`
   102	(`Picard/DegreeZero.lean:229`) does it.  Constructing them here rather than demanding them
   103	of the caller is the whole ergonomic point — a caller who has only `K` cannot produce them,
   104	since `L` does not exist until step 2. -/
   105	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEtAff (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   106	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   107	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   108	    (a : PicEtAff C K) :
   109	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
   110	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
   111	        (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic),
   112	      PicEtAff.map C L a = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) := by
   113	  -- (1) read `a` as a plus class on a presented cover
   114	  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
   115	  | mk E x =>
   116	    -- (2) refine the cover by a finite separable field
   117	    obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
   118	    letI := hLfield
   119	    letI := hLalg
   120	    letI := hLfin
   121	    letI := hLsep
   122	    -- the `k`-structure and the tower are the composite, not a choice
   123	    letI hkL : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
   124	    haveI htow : IsScalarTower k K L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
   125	    -- FORGET the composite's VALUE before going further (I-0161-adjacent hazard, measured
   126	    -- this session).  Keeping it transparent makes the final `exact` substitute a composite
   127	    -- algebra term for the existential's variable, and every `overSpec k L` /
   128	    -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` in the goal is then rechecked against a differently-spelled
   129	    -- instance — that defeq does not terminate inside 1600000 heartbeats.  `htow` is a
   130	    -- `have`, so it has already forgotten the value it was proved from; nothing downstream
   131	    -- needs it.
   132	    clear_value hkL
   133	    -- (3) the refinement is the presentation
   134	    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom C x ℓ
   135	    exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hLalg, htow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM⟩
   136	
   137	variable (C) in
   138	/-- **The splitting theorem in the `picEt` spelling** — the form every consumer of
   139	`IsSplitWitness` meets, since the split predicate is stated on
   140	`PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)`.  Immediate from
   141	`exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` at `a := picEtAffineEquiv C K μ`; kept separate so that the
   142	heavy elaboration of the previous theorem is not re-run through the affine comparison. -/
   143	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEt {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   144	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
